questions.q: What is the battery’s main job in a vehicle?
options: To supply the strong current that drives the starter motor when starting, and back up the systems when the engine is off
To cool the engine
To extend the life of the tyres
To regulate oil pressure
questions.explain: The battery supplies the strong current needed to run the starter motor when starting, and feeds the vehicle’s systems when the engine is off. While driving, it is the alternator that feeds and recharges it.

questions.q: What can shorten a battery’s life?
options: Long, regular drives
Short trips only, and lights left on
Driving on a expressway
A regular oil change
questions.explain: Short trips do not let the battery charge fully, and a light left on drains it — two habits that significantly shorten its life.

questions.q: Why must you never bring an open flame or a lit cigarette near a battery?
options: There is no real risk, it is just excessive caution
Because the battery gives off flammable hydrogen gas, especially while charging or jump-starting
It is only forbidden by the vehicle’s registration document, with no safety reason
It only causes cosmetic damage
questions.explain: A battery gives off flammable hydrogen gas, especially while charging. A flame, a spark or a cigarette near it can cause an explosion.

questions.q: What drives the alternator?
options: The ignition switch alone
A drive belt connected to a pulley on the crankshaft
The battery itself
The engine’s oil pressure
questions.explain: The alternator is driven by the drive belt, connected to a pulley on the crankshaft, and so produces electricity for as long as the engine runs.

questions.q: What does it mean when the charge (battery) warning light comes on while driving?
options: Oil pressure has dropped
The engine is overheating
The battery is fully charged
The charging system has stopped feeding the vehicle, and it now runs on the battery alone
questions.explain: The charge warning light warns that the alternator is not charging, usually because of a fault in it or in the drive belt. From this moment the vehicle runs only on what is left in the battery.

questions.q: The charge warning light and the engine temperature warning light come on together. What could explain both?
options: A low fuel level
The same torn drive belt, which drives both the alternator and the water pump
There is no connection between the two lights
A fault in the dashboard light itself only
questions.explain: In many vehicles the same belt drives both the alternator and the water pump. A torn belt can cause both a loss of charging and overheating.

questions.q: What does the immobiliser do?
options: Stops the engine from starting when it does not recognise the correct chip in the key
Cools the starter motor
Adjusts the valves
Only supplies electricity to the lights
questions.explain: The immobiliser stops the engine from starting when it does not recognise the matching chip in the key or the fob, even if the rest of the electrics are fine — a protection against theft.

questions.q: What is the starter motor’s job?
options: To regulate the engine’s temperature
To turn the crankshaft fast enough for the combustion cycle to begin
To clean the fuel before it enters the engine
To supply the vehicle with constant electricity while driving
questions.explain: The starter motor is a powerful electric motor that turns the crankshaft, through the flywheel, until the engine catches and starts running under its own power.

questions.q: Why must you not keep trying to start a vehicle over and over when it does not catch?
options: Because the law forbids it
Because it can drain the battery and overheat the starter motor
Because it automatically cleans the injectors
There is no problem trying as many times as you like in a row
questions.explain: Repeated starting attempts in a row drain the battery and can overheat the starter motor. Pause between attempts.

questions.q: Why will most manual vehicles not start unless the clutch pedal is pressed all the way down?
options: To save fuel
There is no reason — it is arbitrary
To prevent an unexpected lurch of the vehicle the moment it starts
To pre-heat the clutch
questions.explain: A safety switch prevents starting with a gear engaged, so the vehicle does not lurch forward or backward the moment the starter motor turns the engine.

questions.q: What is a fuse’s job?
options: To blow and break a circuit when too much current flows through it, before the wiring is damaged
To increase the current in a circuit
To adjust the angle of the headlights
To charge the battery
questions.explain: A fuse is a deliberately weak link: it blows and breaks the circuit when the current is too high, so the wire itself does not heat up and burn.

questions.q: Which fuse may you use to replace a blown one?
options: Any fuse that is close at hand
Always one with a higher rating, to be safe
Only one with the same rating (the same colour and number)
It does not matter — any fuse will work
questions.explain: Replace a blown fuse only with one of the same rating. A fuse with a higher rating will not protect the circuit in time and can cause a fire.

questions.q: You have fitted a new fuse and it blows again straight away. What is right to do?
options: Connect a piece of metal wire instead of the fuse
Fit a fuse with a higher rating until it holds
Take it to a garage to diagnose the real fault in the circuit, instead of continuing to replace fuses
Ignore it — it happens at random
questions.explain: A fuse that blows again straight away marks a real fault in the circuit (such as a short). Continuing to replace fuses without fixing the cause can cause a fire.

questions.q: What does a relay do?
options: Measures the fuel level
Charges the battery directly
Uses a weak current to activate a separate circuit carrying a much stronger current
Breaks a circuit when the current is too high, like a fuse
questions.explain: A relay is an electrically operated switch: a weak current activates it, and it closes a separate circuit carrying a strong current, for consumers such as the starter motor or the fans.

questions.q: When is it correct and appropriate to use fog lights?
options: To signal a turn
Only when visibility is genuinely poor — fog, heavy rain or dust
Only on ordinary urban driving
On every night drive, as extra lighting
questions.explain: Fog lights are strong and low, and can dazzle other drivers in normal visibility. Use them only when visibility is genuinely poor.

questions.q: When does the reverse light come on?
options: Every time you press the brake
When you switch on the hazard lights
Permanently during night driving
Only when reverse gear is engaged
questions.explain: The reverse light (white) comes on only when reverse gear is engaged, warning those around that the vehicle is about to move backwards.

questions.q: What is the benefit of daytime running lights (DRL)?
options: To act as fog lights
To save fuel
To replace the brake lights
To make the vehicle visible from a distance even in strong daylight
questions.explain: Daytime running lights come on automatically during the day so the vehicle is visible from a distance even in strong natural light, not as a substitute for other lights.

questions.q: Why is it recommended to replace both headlight bulbs on one side at the same time, even if only one has failed?
options: Both bulbs wear out at roughly the same rate, avoiding another garage visit soon
To change the colour of the light
It is required by law in every case
A new bulb on its own will not work at all
questions.explain: Both bulbs wear out at roughly the same rate, so replacing them together saves another trip to the garage in the near future.

questions.q: What is the first connection in the correct order for jump-starting?
options: Red clamp to the negative terminal of the donor battery
Black clamp to the negative terminal of the flat battery
Red clamp to the positive terminal of the flat battery
Black clamp to bare metal on the flat-battery vehicle
questions.explain: You start with the red clamp to the positive (+) terminal of the flat battery, and only afterwards to the donor battery.

questions.q: Where do you connect the last black clamp, on the vehicle with the flat battery?
options: To a bare metal point on the engine block or chassis, not to the battery’s negative terminal
To the positive terminal of the flat battery
There is no need for a fourth connection at all
To the negative terminal of the flat battery itself
questions.explain: The last black clamp connects to bare metal on the engine block or chassis — not directly to the flat battery’s negative terminal — to prevent a spark near the hydrogen gas it gives off.

questions.q: In what order do you disconnect the jump leads when you are finished?
options: The same order you connected them in
Disconnect all of them at once
In reverse order: first both black clamps, then the two red ones
The order of disconnecting does not matter
questions.explain: Disconnect in exactly the reverse order from connecting: first both black clamps, and only then both red clamps.

questions.q: What do you do after the vehicle with the flat battery has caught and started running?
options: Disconnect both vehicles immediately and drive off as normal with no further check
Switch it off immediately to save fuel
Drive for at least half an hour so the battery recharges, and it is a good idea to check the charging system at a garage
No further action is needed
questions.explain: Driving for at least half an hour lets the battery recharge. It is also worth having the battery and the charging system checked at a garage, to prevent it happening again.

questions.q: You find that the flat battery is swollen and cracked. What is right to do?
options: Do not try to jump-start it yourself — get professional help
Connect the leads in reverse to compensate for the damage
Jump-start it as normal, with extra care
Wipe the crack with a cloth and carry on
questions.explain: A battery that is swollen, cracked, frozen or leaking is a real hazard (acid, explosion). Do not deal with it yourself — get professional help.

questions.q: What is an alternative to jump leads from a second vehicle, for starting a vehicle with a flat battery?
options: A portable jump starter — a battery pack with its own leads
Connecting directly to a household electrical socket
Replacing the tyres
Adding more fuel
questions.explain: A portable jump starter is a battery pack with its own leads, which lets you start a vehicle with a flat battery without needing a second vehicle as a donor.
